title: build: depend on @babel/parser directly
body:
Closes #205 --- ## Agent summary The StyleX plugin imports `@babel/parser`, but that package is only a transitive dependency. `package.json` now lists `@babel/parser` as a direct dependency. Test changes: none ## Caveats **0 departures** **0 loose ends**
1 assumption - The issue left the version open. The branch uses `"^7.29.9"`, the version the lockfile already resolved.
## Conceptual Changes **None** ## Proof 1. ✅ A clean `bun install` in a new worktree, with the default linker, passes `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test`.
Before and after - **Asserts:** a clean install with the default linker passes typecheck and the tests. - **Before:** with `--linker isolated`, the base lacks a top-level `@babel/parser`, and `bun run typecheck` exits 1. - **After:** a clean clone has no `node_modules`. `bunfig.toml` sets no linker. `bun install` on bun 1.4.3 exits 0. It installs 92 packages. `@babel/parser` sits at the top level. `flock /tmp/project-flow-suite.lock nice taskset -c 0-3 bun run typecheck` exits 0. It prints "No type errors in 82 files". `flock /tmp/project-flow-suite.lock nice taskset -c 0-3 bun run test` exits 0. It reports 451 pass, 0 fail, 18 files. With `--linker isolated`, HEAD has `@babel/parser` at the top level. Typecheck exits 0.
## Merge Danger **Door:** ↔️ two-way **Blast Radius:** 📦 module - A bad range can pull a `@babel/parser` the StyleX plugin cannot import, and then typecheck fails for every clean install.
How The StyleX plugin imports `@babel/parser` from the install root. The caret range can move within Babel 7. The lockfile pins the resolved version until the next install updates it.
